6. Restoration must close both inventory and geometry
Chemical stock

The 10 mL bath initially requires approximately:

1.2485 g CuSO₄·5H₂O.
0.9799 g pure H₃PO₄.
Polished water to measured final volume.

The functional copper inventory is approximately:

Location	Initial copper
Dissolved copper	317.73 mg
Counterelectrode grid	313.60 mg
Total functional stock	631.33 mg

The bath volume supplies circulation and limits a one-seam concentration excursion to approximately 1.6%. It must not be enlarged to make material loss appear small.

A paid copper-deposition/water-oxidation operation restores the counter mass and proton balance. It uses a separate Ti/IrO₂ restoration electrode included in the cart. Under the introduced yields, this produces approximately 1.66 µg H₂ and 13.19 µg O₂ per attempt and consumes 14.85 µg water.

No theoretical recovered energy is credited.

Active-material accounting

The inventory also contains approximately 51 mg patterned nickel, 0.65 mg Ir tip coating, the actual weighed mask and primer, seals and spring material. The flexing links alone contribute approximately 1.47 g per receiver pair.

These materials require separate functional tracking. Steel backing cannot compensate for complete loss of a critical Ir film.

5.443 mg Cu=0.862% of functional copper stock.

That can fit the copper mass limit. It is also equivalent to 104% of one instantaneous seam’s copper mass—a useful stricter diagnostic, but not the only legitimate inventory definition.

No mask, seed, spring or interface seal is scheduled for replacement during the 500-service qualification campaign. Their survival has not been demonstrated.

A particularly important blank is copper deposition without applied current accompanied by nickel dissolution. That would indicate consumption of exposed nickel through displacement chemistry, not successful renewable operation.
